transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this brief meeting because we have one mobile bariatric lift available for immediate assignment, and both the North and South inpatient units have patients whose transfer plans are being reviewed for use of the lift. Before I can finalize the assignment, hospital policy requires us to hold a brief equipment-readiness check with physical therapy, facilities, nursing education, and infection prevention. I'd like to go around and hear from each of you on readiness so we can determine the best path forward. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I'd like to start by sharing my physical therapy assessments for both patients. The South unit patient failed the sit-to-stand assessment and requires a full-body bariatric lift for every bed-to-chair transfer. The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt. Based on these clinical findings, the South unit patient has a clear and immediate need for the bariatric lift, while the North unit patient has a safe alternative transfer method available.

transcript.text: I'd like to share some important facilities information. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, which has a 48-inch turning radius. This fits South room 412's 50-inch doorway, but North room 318 has a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate this lift. Additionally, the charger must be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. So from a facilities standpoint, the lift can only be safely used on the South unit.

transcript.text: From a nursing education standpoint, I need to share important staffing information for the South unit. Three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation, and hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer. Their available coverage is 07:00-19:00 daily. This means the South unit can support lift transfers during those hours, but transfers outside that window would not have sufficient validated staff available.

commitments.detail: Lift transfers for South room 412 are restricted to 07:00-19:00 daily, with two competency-validated staff members present for every transfer.
A dedicated extra-large sling labeled for South room 412 must be used, and a documented disinfecting wipe-down must occur after each transfer.
Charger to be installed in the South 4B equipment alcove; lift is not to be relocated to North unit due to 36-inch doorway incompatibility.
North unit patient to continue with two-person stand-pivot transfer with gait belt as the safe alternative method; reassess if clinical status changes.
